correctness.rationale: Classified forests by final hub partition: three separate hubs admit no branching peripheral; a pair block has one degree-two branch; the full block needs either one triple or two different pair masks. Each branch consumes one or two of the only two available hub mergers. In the pair-block case each ordinary peripheral has component attachment weights 2v and v, so two ordinary marked terminals have connected weight 5v²; in the full-block case every nonisolated terminal is connected to its partner if that partner is also nonisolated. Unmarked nonbranching vertices have factor A=1+3v. These checks confirm the census mechanism, and a fresh exact symbolic census reproduced Z=A^(m+2)P, Z_X=3v²A^m Q and Z_XY=3v⁴A^(m−2)S, including m=0,1 where impossible exceptions have zero multiplicity. Terminal exchangeability gives Z_Y=Z_X. Expansion verifies SP−3Q²=4vR with R coefficientwise nonnegative and R(0,0)=4. The denominator is positive at every allowed parameter. Full independent edge-subset checks give 1,856, 9,984 and 51,712 forests at v=1 for n=4,5,6, respectively; the all-n conclusion rests on the symbolic classification, not those finite checks.
residual_risks: The theorem is for four distinct peripheral terminals and common v>0; no extension to unequal fugacities or other terminal placements is certified.

value.rationale: This proves an all-size all-fugacity case of a natural four-terminal question on a family with overlapping cycles, where edge correlation results do not settle connectivity. The nonnegative coefficient certificate demonstrates strictness in the full parameter range, including regimes inaccessible to a high-fugacity argument. The fixed hub count makes it tractable without reducing it to an isolated numerical example.
residual_risks: No conclusion here about general graphs, or about application to edge events, unequal weights or general random-cluster parameters.
